title: feat(release): publish the browser (wasm32) build under /app/ on the Pages site
body:
## What changed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
  - New job **`wasm`** (ubuntu-24.04, `contents: read`, 45 min timeout): `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`, apt `clang-18` / `llvm-18` (CC/AR for wasm32 set via `GITHUB_ENV`), `bash web/build-app-wasm.sh --release`, `web/check-app-page.sh target/web`, an `if: always()` warning if `Cargo.lock` is left modified (#949), upload `target/web/` as artifact `wasm-app`.
  - Job **`site`** now `needs: [wasm]` with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` (the pattern `publish` uses). After `zola build` it downloads `wasm-app` only when `needs.wasm.result == 'success'`, replaces `site/public/app/` with it and runs the check on the Pages artifact's `app/`; otherwise it emits `::warning::Browser build missing: ...` and keeps the site's own `app/` page.
  - `pages` is unchanged. No new trigger: still `vX.Y.0` tags and hand-run `workflow_dispatch` (which builds and deploys nothing).
- `web/check-app-page.sh` (new, runs locally too): the four files are present and non-empty, the `.wasm` starts with the wasm magic, no `src=`/`href=`/import-map value/`import`/`fetch`/`new URL`/`new Worker` names a root-absolute (`/x`), protocol-relative (`//x`) or `http(s):` URL, and no `SharedArrayBuffer`.
- Site: `content/app.md` + `templates/app.html` are the page at `app/` when the site has no browser build (a local preview, or a release whose wasm build failed): it says so and why, so the link is never a 404. The front page (`templates/index.html`, because only the templates read `version.toml`) gets "Try CamCraft in your browser" with the version, WebGL2, and what does not work yet (#31: no file picker, no playback without threads, no WebGPU, views needing desktop GPU features say so). `guide/first-run.md` gets a short "Trying it in the browser first" section. The old "coming" paragraph is gone. One `.button` CSS rule.
- `docs/decisions/1103-wasm-app-on-pages.md`: path layout, failure behaviour, #949 handling, no new trigger, no wasm-opt.

No change to `web/index.html`, `wasi_shim.js` or the build script: every URL was already relative (`./wasi_shim.js` in the import map and module script, `./camcraft-ui.js`, and the glue's `new URL('camcraft-ui_bg.wasm', import.meta.url)`). The check now pins that.

## Review fixes (head 1e345767, after merging origin/main)

- **The front page claims only what was deployed.** The `site` job appends `app = true|false` to the gitignored `site/version.toml` before `zola build`; `true` only when the `wasm` job succeeded, the artifact downloaded (now `continue-on-error`) and `web/check-app-page.sh` passes on it. `templates/base.html` reads it as `app`; `templates/index.html` shows one of three lines. The first-run page is Markdown and cannot read the flag, so it says "when this site's release has a browser version" and points at the front page.
- **The check in `site` is never fatal for the docs.** It now runs twice in `site`: on the downloaded artifact (decides the flag), and on the copy at `public/app/` (proves the Pages artifact holds it). A failure of the second drops the copy, flips the flag to `false` and rebuilds the site (about 0.3 s), with the same `::warning::Browser build missing: ...` annotation. Kept rather than moved to the `wasm` job only, because the issue's "Done means" asks for a check on the Pages artifact.
- **Plain wording:** "Open CamCraft X in your browser", "needs a browser with WebGL2 (a current Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari)" once, no "wasm32"/"shell" on the site.

### What a visitor sees

| Case | Front page | `/app/` | Run |
|---|---|---|---|
| wasm ok, both checks pass | button "Open CamCraft X in your browser" + "same release, nothing to install, needs WebGL2 (...)" + the early-version limits | the app | green |
| wasm job failed (or artifact did not download / pre-check failed) | "The browser version of CamCraft X is not available: it did not build for this release. Use the desktop downloads." (link to `/app/`) + limits | page "CamCraft in the browser": not part of this copy of the site, why, desktop downloads | `::warning::Browser build missing: ...`; docs and release deploy |
| copy at `public/app/` fails the check in `site` | same as the failed case (flag flipped, site rebuilt) | same stand-in page | `::warning::Browser build missing: its copy at app/ failed ...`; docs deploy |
| local preview (no `version.toml`) | "CamCraft in the browser comes with a released copy of this site; this local preview does not have it." | stand-in page | - |

Verified: pinned Zola 0.23.6 in WSL, `zola build` + `zola check` pass in all three flag states (none / true / false), front-page text read back from the built HTML for each; the `Build the site` step's body run in WSL with a passing and a failing fixture as `/tmp/wasm-app`: passing -> app/ holds the four files, `app = true`, button shown; failing -> warning printed, `app = false`, site rebuilt, app/ is the stand-in, "not available" shown. The real build output was checked before (first round); the worktree was removed after that push, so the second round used fixtures and did not rebuild the wasm.

## Wiring

```
linux, macos, windows, freebsd ─┬─> aur/snap/flatpak ─┐
                                └─────────────────────┴─> publish (release page) ─┐
wasm ──[artifact wasm-app = target/web/]──> site (!cancelled)                       ├─> pages (tag only; site + publish success)
          app = wasm ok && artifact && check(artifact)  -> version.toml `app = ...`  │
          zola build -> public/app/ = app.md stand-in                                │
          app:      public/app/ := wasm-app; check fails -> drop, app=false, rebuild │
          no app:   ::warning:: Browser build missing; stand-in stays ───────────────┘
          upload-pages-artifact(site/public)
```

## #949 (Cargo.lock)

Not stacked on #1009. The wasm build runs on its own runner and only `target/web/` leaves it, so a rewritten lock cannot reach any package or the site. The script on main already restores the lock via its EXIT trap (locally: `git status` clean after the build). The workflow warns if it ever is not. #1009 merges independently in either order.

## Readings (point 5)

- **Local build:** `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` in the worktree on Windows (Git Bash, clang 21 msys2) - **exit 0, 7 min 09 s wall**, fresh `target/` (sccache was on PATH, so some third-party crates may have been cache hits): camcraft-app ~2 m 46 s, camcraft-ui cdylib ~2 m 33 s, wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.129 install 1 m 15 s. `Cargo.lock` clean afterwards.
- **Sizes:** `camcraft-ui_bg.wasm` 29,878,727 B (28.5 MiB), gzip -9 8,983,088 B (8.6 MiB); `camcraft-ui.js` 154 KB; whole Pages artifact ~29 MB. Pages limits: 100 MB/file, 1 GB site - well inside.
- **Billed minutes per cut (estimate):** the `wasm` job on a cold 4-vCPU ubuntu-24.04 runner, no cache: apt ~1 min, wasi sysroot + cargo fetch ~1 min, two release builds + wasm-bindgen-cli ~10-15 min -> **about 12-18 billed Linux minutes (1x)**; the `site` job grows by seconds (artifact download + copy). Not measured on a runner.
- **wasm-opt:** not used - binaryen has no version+checksum-pinned download here, and the size does not need it.
- **Threads / COOP-COEP:** Pages sends no COOP/COEP headers. The glue and shim contain no `SharedArrayBuffer` (checked by the script), and the build has no atomics/threads target feature, so nothing relies on cross-origin isolation.

## Tests / checks run

- `bash web/check-app-page.sh target/web` on the real output: ok.
- Simulated Pages artifact: pinned Zola v0.23.6 (linux musl, workflow's sha256 verified) in WSL Ubuntu-24.04, `zola build --base-url https://someone.github.io/Fork-Repo` -> app links resolve to `https://someone.github.io/Fork-Repo/app/` on the front page and first-run page; then `public/app/` replaced by `target/web` and the check run on it: ok.
- `zola check`: passes (11 pages, 0 orphans).
- Check script against a bad fixture (root-absolute import map, `/x` fetch, `//cdn` import, `/a.wasm` `new URL`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, non-wasm `.wasm`): all 7 reported, exit 1. Good fixture: exit 0.
- Workflow YAML parsed (python yaml): jobs, `wasm` permissions read-only, `site` needs/if, triggers unchanged. actionlint not available (no checksummed download found) - not run.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: "nothing in crates/ changed: no tests to run" (0 steps).

## Not exercised

- **The workflow did not run** (no tag, no dispatch - zero Actions minutes). The `wasm` job's Linux path (apt clang-18/llvm-18, `CC_`/`AR_` env, wasm-bindgen-cli build on Linux) is unproven until the next release tag; the local build was Windows.
- No browser was launched; loading `/Camcraft/app/` in Chrome/Firefox is unproven here (#31's earlier headless Chrome run covered the same page from a local server).
- The failure branches ran only as the step's shell body under WSL with fixtures, not inside Actions; `continue-on-error` on the download and the `needs.wasm.result` wiring are read, not run.

Fork synced: n/a (canonical repo, main a0891091).

Changelog: The release workflow builds the browser (wasm32) shell and publishes it at `/app/` on the GitHub Pages site, linked from the front page and the first-run guide; a failed browser build leaves a page saying so and never withholds the docs or the release (#1103)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1103
